phase_a_classification: Three-guide adiabatic splitter/coupler: a central guide narrows while two symmetric side guides widen, then the side guides fan out as outputs.

pre_geometry_derivation.rule_based_adaptation: Set all access/output waveguides to the stack single_mode_width_um = 1.0. Set central terminal and side tip widths to min_feature_um = 0.4. The minimum legal coupled edge gap is 0.4, which fixes the symmetric coupled rail centers at +/-1.1 um because 1.0/2 + 0.4 + 0.4/2 = 1.1.
pre_geometry_derivation.physics_reasoning: This remains a symmetric mode-evolution splitter. Transmission is controlled by adiabatic following of the even mode from the central guide into the symmetric side-guide pair; split balance should be exactly 0.5 for a symmetric device. The SOI cap showed branch-gap detuning is very sensitive, so the SiN first call stays symmetric and spends the length budget on transfer rather than biasing balance.
pre_geometry_derivation.initial_prediction: The midpoint even-mode separation is much smaller than SOI, so this first shot is length-limited even at the full 150 um footprint. I predict total transmission around 0.82, with the main uncertainty being whether the lower-index SiN mode extension makes the adiabatic transfer more forgiving than the local effective-index spacing suggests. The symmetric geometry should give split_fraction near 0.50.

iterations.reasoning: Initial SiN measurement candidate. The device is symmetric to avoid the SOI detuning overshoot failure mode, all waveguide/tip/gap dimensions satisfy the 1.0 um width and 0.4 um min-feature rules, and the 149 um taper uses nearly the entire 150 um device budget for mode transfer. The fixture is economical: it starts at the device outputs, fans to 6 um separation over 20 um, and adds only 4 um straight stubs with probes halfway into the stubs.

final_outcome.calibration_gap: The first-call T prediction of 0.82 was too pessimistic. The local cross-section effective-index spacing was useful for choosing a long symmetric taper, but it over-penalized adiabaticity in this low-contrast SiN geometry; the measured mode evolution is much more forgiving and achieved T=0.974 within 149 um.
